# data

> A small, dependency-free reactive data library for TypeScript/JavaScript. Wrap any object or array in `$()` to get a reactive handle; derive views with chainable operators; bind them to the DOM with `render`. Like crossfilter's incremental aggregation with Solid-style fine-grained DOM updates. Every row has a stable key, every change is a keyed delta, and every write settles the graph in one commit. Work is proportional to the path that changed, not the size of the data.

## Quick start

Install: `npm install data`

```js
import { $, value } from 'data'                 // the one entry: operators registered on import

const rows = $([{ name: 'a', n: 1 }, { name: 'b', n: 9 }])
const big  = rows.filter(r => r.n > 3)          // derived reactive view (predicate only)
console.log(big[value])                         // read raw with the `value` symbol — a dense snapshot
rows.get(0).set('n', 10)                        // writes are METHODS; views update incrementally
```

## Imports

- `data` — THE entry: `$`, `value`, `batch`, every operator, `render`/`el`/`text`/`list`/`bind`, `HTML`/`SVG` builders, JSX (`h`, `Fragment`, `For`, `ErrorBoundary`), `component`/`onCleanup`/`boundary`, and the seam (`fromAsync`, `exportContract`, `InMemoryBacking`). Use this.
- `data/jsx-runtime` / `data/jsx-dev-runtime` — automatic JSX (`"jsxImportSource": "data"`); thin re-exports of the main bundle (one module instance).
- `data/devtools` — opt-in inspection helpers + overlay panel (side-effecting import; `?nopanel` opts out).
- `data/v3`, `data/v3/jsx-runtime`, `data/v3/devtools` — transitional aliases for the same files; prefer the bare names.
- `data/v2` (+ `/lean`, `/full`, `/render`, `/devtools`, `/jsx-runtime`) — the frozen pre-flip v2 engine. Never mix `data` and `data/v2` handles: different engines, different `value` symbols.

## Core API

- `$(objectOrArray)` → a `Data` handle. Read raw with `proxy[value]` (the exported `value` symbol) or `proxy.snapshot()` — NOT `proxy.value` (a child named "value"). Snapshots are DENSE (no holes, no `undefined` slots).
- `proxy.get(key)` → the child handle (collision-free; a data key named `length`/`filter` must use `get`). Property sugar works for non-reserved names. `for (const row of view)` iterates rows.
- Writes are METHODS: `set(key, v)`, `child.update(v)`, `insert(row, at?)` (returns the minted key), `child.remove()`, `patch([[k1, row1], [k2, row2]])` ([key, row] TUPLE pairs, one commit). Bare assignment (`proxy.x = v`), `delete proxy.x`, and `proxy[value] = v` all THROW with a message naming the replacement. Deep paths compose: `proxy.a.b.c.update(1)`.
- `batch(() => { ...writes })` — N writes, ONE commit; net-zero changes annihilate.
- `proxy.connect(arr)` pushes `{ type, key, value, at? }` records; `connect(obj, 'prop')` mirrors; `connect(anchor, fn)` calls `fn(record)`. All return a `SubscriptionHandle` — references are STRONG, call `.dispose()`.
- `view.mirror()` → a re-pointable slot: chain downstream ops off it once, `slot.set(otherView)` re-points as one consolidated diff. `view.dispose()` detaches a view permanently — dispose transients.
- `child.raf()` (child handles only) → coalescing writer, one commit per frame, `.flush()` on pointerup. `first()`/`last()` → the edge child handle.
- `render(el, ast)` → a `RenderHandle` (`.dispose()`). Build with `HTML.div(...)`/`SVG.path(...)` builders or JSX. Reactive text is `text(view, fn?)`; reactive props are `bind(view, fn?)`; iteration is ONLY `list(view, (row, key) => ...)` / `<For each={view}>{(row, key) => ...}</For>`, kept the sole child of its container. Row fns receive PLAIN rows; listeners bind once — handlers read current state through the source (`items.get(id)[value]`). Props use literal `class`/`for`/`style` strings (no `className`, no style objects).

## Operators (chain off any handle; derived views are read-only)

- Filter: `filter(fn)` — PREDICATE ONLY; `between('col', [lo, hi])` or `between('col', bounds.get('col'))` (one reactive tuple handle; O(Δ) brush walk); `gt`/`lt`/`gte`/`lte('col', n)` (threshold may be a reactive handle).
- Sort/limit (ordered views — materialize as ARRAYS in rank order, row keys are source keys): `az`/`za('col' | cmpFn, n?)` (bounded window; `n` may be reactive — the window resizes in place), `top(n)`, `limit(n)`. `za`/`az` REQUIRE a column or comparator — numeric `za(5)` throws; use `top(5)`/`limit(5)`. No `reverse`/`page`/`join` (reserved, throw).
- Aggregate (scalar handles — no children): `length()`, `sum`/`avg`/`max`/`min(col?)` (col may be reactive), `some`/`every(fn)`. Empty set: `sum` → 0, `avg`/`max`/`min` → undefined.
- Histogram/buckets: `length(fn)` → `{ value: N }` buckets (emptied buckets persist at `{ value: 0 }`); `group(fn)` → member objects (prunes empties); `distinct(fn?)` → unique projected values.
- Transform: `map(fn)`, `to(fn)` (whole-snapshot → scalar), `reduce(fn, init)` or incremental `reduce(add, remove, init)` (init may be a thunk, never a reactive handle — throws).
- Set algebra: `intersect`/`union`/`except(...views)` — operands are VIEWS (`src.intersect(viewA, viewB)`), not object maps.
- Misc: `tap(fn)` (effects run after the graph settles), `keys()`, `values()`.

## Common gotchas

- **Writes are methods only.** `proxy.set('x', 1)` / `proxy.x.update(1)` / `proxy.get(k).remove()` / `patch([[k, row], ...])`. Bare assignment, `delete`, and `[value] =` throw (the error names the replacement). Read raw with `proxy[value]`, never `proxy.value`.
- **`filter` takes a predicate only.** `filter(r => r.status === 'open')`. The v2 `filter('key', v)` / `filter({k: v})` forms throw at construction. For a reactive threshold use `gt`/`lt`/`gte`/`lte`/`between` (those take reactive handles); for reactive re-selection use a transient filter + `mirror()` + `dispose()`.
- **`length(fn)` buckets are `{ value: N }` wrappers.** Read a count via `counts.get(k)[value].value` or `counts.get(k).get('value')[value]`; in a binding, `text(counts.get(k), b => b?.value ?? 0)`. Emptied buckets persist at `{ value: 0 }`.
- **References are strong — nothing unsubscribes by GC.** `connect` returns a `SubscriptionHandle` you must `.dispose()`; dispose transient views after re-pointing away from them; `mirror()` is the re-pointable slot (`slot.set(view)`); `render()` returns a disposable handle.
- **Know the two shapes.** Ordered views (`az`/`za`/`top`/`limit`) materialize as arrays in rank order; row/set/bucket operators over an ARRAY-born source materialize as a KEYED OBJECT (`$([...]).filter(fn)[value]` is `{"0": row, "2": row}`) — sort (`.az(col)`) or iterate the handle if you need an array.
